claim: Amazon EFS offers three storage classes: EFS Standard, EFS Infrequent Access and EFS Archive.
question: Which storage classes does Amazon EFS offer?

evidence.quote: Amazon EFS offers three storage classes: EFS Standard, EFS Infrequent Access, and EFS Archive.

claim: EFS Standard is an SSD-powered class designed to deliver sub-millisecond latencies.
question: What latency does EFS Standard deliver?

evidence.quote: Data that is frequently accessed tends to have higher performance needs, so EFS provides an SSD-powered EFS Standard class designed to deliver sub-millisecond latencies.

claim: EFS IA is designed for data accessed only a few times a quarter and EFS Archive for data accessed a few times a year or less; both provide low double-digit millisecond latencies.
question: What access pattern and latency fit EFS IA and EFS Archive?

values.display: a few times a year or less

evidence.quote: For data that’s infrequently accessed, you can use EFS’s two cost-optimized storage classes that provide low double-digit millisecond latencies: EFS Infrequent Access (IA), designed for data accessed only a few times a quarter, and EFS Archive, designed for data accessed a few times a year or less.

claim: EFS IA offers up to 95% lower cost than EFS Standard for infrequently accessed data.
question: How much cheaper is EFS IA than EFS Standard?

qualifiers.scope: EFS IA compared with EFS Standard

evidence.quote: EFS IA offers an up to 95% lower cost than EFS Standard for infrequently accessed data.

claim: EFS Archive offers up to 50% lower cost than EFS Infrequent Access, with a higher request charge when the data is accessed.
question: How much cheaper is EFS Archive than EFS IA?

qualifiers.scope: EFS Archive compared with EFS IA

evidence.quote: Providing a more cost-optimized experience for even colder data, EFS Archive offers an up to 50% lower cost than EFS Infrequent Access, with a higher request charge when that data is accessed.

claim: EFS Archive is optimized for and supported on EFS Regional file systems that use the default Elastic Throughput mode.
question: Which EFS file systems support the Archive class?

evidence.quote: EFS Archive is optimized for and supported on EFS Regional file systems using EFS’s default Elastic Throughput mode.

claim: The default, recommended EFS lifecycle policy tiers files from Standard to IA after 30 consecutive days without access and to Archive after 90 consecutive days without access.
question: What is the default recommended EFS lifecycle policy?

evidence.quote: The default, recommended lifecycle policy will tier files from EFS Standard to EFS IA after 30 consecutive days without access and to EFS Archive after 90 consecutive days without access.

claim: EFS Intelligent-Tiering promotes files from IA and Archive back to Standard when they are accessed, so later reads have the sub-millisecond latencies of EFS Standard.
question: What does EFS Intelligent-Tiering do?

values.display: promote files from EFS IA and EFS Archive back to EFS Standard

evidence.quote: You can also enable EFS Intelligent-Tiering to promote files from EFS IA and EFS Archive back to EFS Standard when they are accessed, which provides subsequent reads of those files with the faster, sub-millisecond latencies of EFS Standard.

claim: Compared with EFS Standard, EFS IA and Archive offer the same throughput and IOPS scalability but with higher first-byte latencies.
question: How do IA and Archive performance differ from Standard?

values.display: the same throughput and IOPS scalability

qualifiers.scope: EFS IA and EFS Archive compared with EFS Standard

evidence.quote: Compared to the EFS Standard class, EFS IA and Archive offer the same throughput and IOPS scalability but with higher first-byte latencies (i.e., low double-digit millisecond read latencies vs. sub-millisecond read latencies on EFS Standard).

claim: EFS IA has no minimum storage duration; data tiered to EFS Archive has a minimum storage duration of 90 days.
question: What minimum storage duration do EFS IA and Archive have?

qualifiers.scope: per file, EFS IA and EFS Archive

evidence.quote: EFS IA has no minimum storage duration. Data that is tiered to EFS Archive has a minimum storage duration of 90 days.

claim: There is no minimum file size for IA or Archive, but files smaller than 128 KiB in these classes incur storage charges as if they were 128 KiB.
question: Is there a minimum file size for EFS IA and Archive?

qualifiers.scope: per file, EFS IA and EFS Archive billing

evidence.quote: There is no minimum file size for IA or Archive, but files tiered to these storage classes that are smaller than 128 KiB will incur storage charges as if they were 128 KiB.

claim: EFS Replication copies file system data into a new or existing file system in the Region of your choice and keeps them synchronized by transferring only incremental changes.
question: What does EFS Replication do?

evidence.quote: Amazon EFS Replication copies your file system data into a new or existing file system in the Region of your choice.
It keeps the two file systems synchronized by automatically transferring only incremental changes without requiring additional infrastructure or a custom process.

claim: EFS Replication is designed to provide a recovery point objective and a recovery time objective of minutes.
question: What RPO and RTO does EFS Replication target?

evidence.quote: EFS Replication is designed to provide a recovery point objective (RPO) and a recovery time objective (RTO) of minutes, helping you meet your compliance and business continuity goals.

claim: While EFS Replication is enabled, applications can use the replica file system in read-only mode for low-latency cross-Region access.
question: Can applications write to an EFS replica while replication is enabled?

evidence.quote: While EFS Replication is enabled, your applications can use the replica file system in read-only mode for low network latency cross-Region access.

claim: EFS Replication does not provide point-in-time consistent replication.
question: Is an EFS replica file system point-in-time consistent?

evidence.quote: EFS Replication doesn't provide point-in-time consistent replication.

claim: EFS Replication publishes the CloudWatch metric TimeSinceLastSync; all changes made to the source at least as of the published time are copied to the replica.
question: Which metric shows how current an EFS replica is?

evidence.quote: EFS Replication publishes a timestamp metric on Amazon CloudWatch called TimeSinceLastSync.

claim: After a disaster you can fail over to the EFS replica and resume business-critical operations within minutes, and later fail back by transferring only incremental changes.
question: How quickly can you resume operations on an EFS replica after a disaster?

evidence.quote: In the event of a disaster, you can failover to your replica file system, and resume operations for your business-critical applications within minutes.

claim: Amazon EFS Backup is powered by AWS Backup, which centrally manages and automates backups of EFS file systems.
question: What powers Amazon EFS Backup?

evidence.quote: Amazon EFS Backup is powered by AWS Backup, which is a fully managed backup service that centrally manages and automates backups of your Amazon EFS file systems.
